verdict: Tyler's revenue rose 9% to $648M as cloud (SaaS) revenue jumped 21%, and record free cash flow of $277M helped fund a $379M share buyback.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $648M vs $596M a year ago; recurring revenue was 88% of the total

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $1.93 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $3.52

kpis.label: SaaS revenue
kpis.note: up 21% YoY — software delivered from Tyler's cloud, the fastest-growing piece

segments.name: Subscriptions
segments.note: Software subscriptions — $242M of cloud (SaaS) revenue, up 21%, plus $220M of transaction-based fees (payments and other per-use charges), up 10%.

segments.name: Maintenance
segments.note: Support and maintenance contracts for software customers run on their own systems — shrinking as customers move to the cloud.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Installing, configuring and training — the people work that goes with new software deals.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Everything else, including hardware and third-party products sold with Tyler's software.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to state and local governments.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day, including much of its stock-based pay.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the software — up 22% YoY as Tyler adds AI features.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of companies and technology Tyler bought in past deals over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $8M, less $4M of interest expense — a net $4M gain below operating income.

takeaways.title: The cloud is doing the growing
takeaways.text: SaaS revenue grew 21% to $242M and subscription revenue overall grew 15%, while old-style maintenance fell 5%. Annualized recurring revenue reached $2.28B, up 11% — most of Tyler's sales now repeat every year.

takeaways.title: Cash flow set a record
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $277M, up 12%, a quarterly record. Tyler spent it two ways: about $28M to buy public-safety software maker CODY Systems, and $379M buying back 1.1 million of its own shares.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit is much higher than GAAP
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $3.52 versus $2.33 GAAP. The gap is mostly $39M of stock-based pay and $25M of amortization of bought software and intangibles — real costs, but ones Tyler's preferred measure leaves out.

footerNote: Amounts are rounded to $M from the statement, which is in thousands (total revenue $647,566K; cost of revenues $329,357K, shown as $330M so the rounded flow ties exactly). Tyler reports revenue by type on its income statement, so those statement lines are the segments here.
